claim: Schönbrunn 2026 tickets: Grand Tour €38 (~75 min, 40 rooms, audio guide), State Apartments/Imperial Tour €28 (~40 min), Classic Pass €44 combines palace with Privy Garden/Maze/Orangery/Gloriette; all palace admission requires fixed time slots booked in advance online and last admission is 45 min before closing.
quote: Classic Pass €44.00... Palace Ticket (Grand Tour) €38.00... State Apartments €28.00... All palace admission requires fixed time slots booked in advance online via imperialtickets.com. Audio guides included with most tickets; last admission is 45 minutes before closing.

claim: Standard Hofburg day ticket bundles Sisi Museum + Imperial Apartments for €20 adult / €12 child with audio guide in 13 languages; the €57 Sisi Ticket combo adds Schönbrunn Grand Tour and the Furniture Museum and is valid one year. The Silver Collection has been closed since 1 April 2023 until further notice.
quote: Standard Day Ticket (Sisi Museum + Imperial Apartments) Adults: €20.00... Sisi Pass... Schönbrunn Palace + Sisi Museum plus the Imperial Apartments in the Vienna Hofburg + the Vienna Furniture Museum: Adults: €57.00... the silver collection will remain closed from April 1, 2023 until further notice.

claim: Belvedere 2026 prices: Upper Belvedere €23, Lower Belvedere €20, combined '2 in 1 Day Ticket' €32; timed slot ticket is mandatory for both buildings. Upper Belvedere opens 09:00 daily, Lower from 10:00.
quote: Upper Belvedere only: €23.00 ... Lower Belvedere only: €20.00 ... Combined '2 in 1 Day Ticket': €32.00 ... The visit to the Upper and Lower Belvedere is only possible with a valid time slot ticket.

claim: Klimt's 'The Kiss' is displayed at the Upper Belvedere on the 1st floor in Gallery 10 as the centerpiece of the Vienna 1900 wing, alongside the world's largest single Klimt collection (24 paintings) — so first-timers with one slot should pick Upper over Lower Belvedere.
quote: showcased in a dedicated gallery with optimal lighting and space for visitors to appreciate its shimmering gold surface up close, located at the Upper Belvedere, 1st Floor, Gallery 10... part of the permanent exhibition at the Wien um 1900 / Vienna 1900 section

claim: Stephansdom South Tower is a 343-step climb (no lift) reaching 67m with panoramic city views including Hofburg, Rathaus and Belvedere; North Tower has a lift and shows the Pummerin bell plus the famed roof tiles but a more limited vista — pick South for athletic visitors, North for accessibility/the bell.
quote: South Tower... 343 steps that wind up a dusky, narrow staircase... splendid views across Vienna in all directions, including landmarks like the Hofburg, Rathaus, and Belvedere Palace... the North Tower offers an accessible alternative with a lift

claim: Entry to the main nave of Stephansdom is free; the catacombs (€8, ~30 min guided), South Tower climb (€6) and North Tower lift (€5) are separate paid add-ons, with an all-access ticket around €29 covering the Dom Museum too.
quote: Access to the main nave of St. Stephen's Cathedral is free of charge, but the South Tower climb and catacomb tour need separate tickets... An all-access ticket for €29 includes the Dom Museum

claim: Stephansdom catacombs tours run hourly-ish Mon–Sat from 10:00 and Sun afternoons; the 25–30 min visit reveals the Ducal Chamber with Rudolf IV's tomb and urns containing Habsburg organs, plus 14th-c. ossuary rooms — short but high-density imperial-history payoff.
quote: lasting about 25-30 minutes... The Ducal Chamber holds the coffins of Rudolf IV and his family, and also contains urns with organs from many high-ranking Habsburgs.

claim: Travel-forum consensus: Imperial Tour and Grand Tour share identical rooms up to the Great Gallery; Grand Tour adds the significant private apartments and is the default pick — only choose Imperial if you have under an hour for the interior.
quote: Both the Imperial Tour and Grand Tour cover the same rooms as far as the ballroom, but the Imperial Tour ends there whereas the Grand Tour continues to some exquisite and significant rooms.

claim: Recommended weekend sequence: Day 1 inside the Ring (Stephansdom at 9am, walk 10 min to Hofburg/Sisi, afternoon Albertina/MQ); Day 2 morning at Schönbrunn at opening (timed slots fill hours ahead), afternoon Belvedere via tram D from Karlsplatz.
quote: Day 1 (City Center)... Start at St. Stephen's Cathedral around 9am, then walk to Hofburg Palace... Day 2... Morning: Schönbrunn Palace - 'Arrive when the palace opens.'... Afternoon: Belvedere Palace (accessible by tram D from Karlsplatz).

claim: Spanish Riding School Morning Exercise (training-only viewing in the Baroque Winter Riding School inside the Hofburg) is the cheaper drop-in option vs full Lipizzaner performances, weekday mornings ~10:00–12:00; book online once dates are firm.
quote: Morning Exercise offers an authentic insight into the training of riders and their Lipizzaners... daily work in the imperial setting of the baroque Winter Riding School, accompanied by classical Viennese music. These sessions are typically held on weekday mornings from around 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM.

claim: Schönbrunn's vast Baroque gardens including the Neptune Fountain and the walk up to the Gloriette hilltop arch are free year-round; only the Gloriette rooftop terrace, Maze, Privy Garden and Orangery need paid tickets — a good fallback if palace slots are sold out.
quote: The Schönbrunn Gardens are free and open year-round, featuring beautiful Baroque landscaping, the Gloriette hill, Roman ruins, and the Neptune Fountain. You can walk up to the Gloriette for free
